title: 少年行·其一
author: 王维
intro: Expensive wine, swaggering young swordsmen, horses tied by a tall tavern under the willows: Wang Wei captures the confidence and generosity of youth in the golden age of the Tang.
analysis: 这是王维《少年行》四首中的第一首，写长安一带意气风发的少年游侠。第一句说新丰的美酒很贵，一斗值十千钱；第二句说咸阳的游侠大多是年轻人。第三句是全诗的核心：大家萍水相逢，因为意气相投，就为了你痛快地喝一杯。“意气”是一种豪爽、讲义气的精神，不在乎钱，也不在乎认识多久。最后一句不写喝酒的场面，只写一个画面：大家把马拴在高楼旁边的垂柳下。高楼、垂柳、骏马，色彩明亮，好像一个电影镜头，热闹和豪气都留给读者去想象。整首诗充满青春的自信和盛唐的昂扬气象。
analysisEn: This is the first of Wang Wei’s four “Songs of Youth”, about the dashing young knights-errant (游侠) of the Chang’an area. The first line tells us the wine of Xinfeng is famous and costly — ten thousand coins a measure. The second says that most of the knights of Xianyang are young men. The third line is the heart of the poem: they have only just met, but because their spirits click (意气), they drink to each other without a second thought. 意气 is a mix of boldness, generosity and loyalty — not caring about money, and not needing years of friendship before you trust someone. Then, instead of describing the party, the last line gives a single picture: the horses tied up beneath the drooping willows beside a tall tavern. Tall building, green willows, fine horses — bright colours, like a shot in a film, and the noise and laughter upstairs are left to our imagination. The whole poem breathes the confidence of youth and the high spirits of the Tang at its height.
background: Wang Wei (701–761) is usually thought to have written the four “Songs of Youth” when he was young himself. “Song of Youth” (少年行) was an old yuefu title used by many poets for scenes of bold young men.
pronunciation: 斗十千：斗 dǒu（量词）。多少年：少 shào（少年）。为君饮：为 wèi（替、给）。系马：系 jì（拴，不读 xì）。
version: 采用通行版本，为《少年行四首》的第一首。

lines.py: xīn fēng měi jiǔ dǒu shí qiān
lines.lit: Xinfeng’s fine wine costs ten thousand a measure;
lines.en: Xinfeng’s wine is fine — ten thousand coins a jug;

lines.py: xián yáng yóu xiá duō shào nián
lines.lit: Xianyang’s knights-errant are mostly young men.
lines.en: Xianyang’s swordsmen are nearly all young.

lines.py: xiāng féng yì qì wèi jūn yǐn
lines.lit: Meeting, in high spirits, I drink for you;
lines.en: We’ve only just met, but our spirits match — I drink to you!

lines.py: jì mǎ gāo lóu chuí liǔ biān
lines.lit: we tie our horses by the tall building, beside the drooping willows.
lines.en: Our horses wait, tied by the tall tavern under the willows.

words.en: Song of Youth (an old song title)
words.note: 行：古诗的一种体裁，如《琵琶行》。

words.en: Xinfeng, near Chang’an, famous for wine

words.note: 古代量器；今天还说“车载斗量”。
古代指青年男子；现代汉语多指十岁到十六岁左右的孩子。
现代汉语“意气风发”“意气相投”。

words.en: to drink for you / to you

words.note: 系：拴、打结，读 jì，如“系鞋带”。

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: 昂贵的美酒和痛快的畅饮，写出少年游侠的豪爽大方。
imagery.en: Costly wine drunk freely shows the young swordsmen’s boldness and generosity.

imagery.name: 马
imagery.zh: 骏马是游侠的伙伴，拴在楼下，暗示主人正在楼上畅饮。
imagery.en: Horses are a swordsman’s companions; tied below, they hint at their masters drinking upstairs.

imagery.name: 楼
imagery.zh: 高楼是热闹的酒楼，青春和豪情都在里面。
imagery.en: The tall building is a lively tavern, full of youth and high spirits.

imagery.name: 柳
imagery.zh: 青青垂柳给画面添上明亮的颜色，衬出春天般的青春气息。
imagery.en: Green drooping willows brighten the picture with a spring-like freshness of youth.
